insights.summary: NVIDIA delivered exceptional Q1 FY2027 results with revenue of $81.6B (+85% YoY) and net income of $58.3B (+211% YoY), driven by strong Blackwell ramp and diversification beyond hyperscalers into AI Clouds, industrial, and enterprise customers. insights.summary: NVIDIA delivered strong FY2026 results with $215.9B revenue (+65% YoY) and $120.1B net income (+65% YoY), driven by Blackwell AI platform demand across data center, gaming, and professional visualization. However, management tone is distinctly cautious due to multiple structural headwinds: a $4.5B H20 inventory charge from April 2025 export controls, effective foreclosure from the China market, complex and shifting global export restrictions that undermine competitive positioning, and significant uncertainty around future regulatory changes. Gross margins compressed 380 bps to 71.1% due to Blackwell full-scale datacenter transition and H20 charges, while capex is expected to increase materially in FY2027.
keyQuotes: As of the end of fiscal year 2026, we were effectively foreclosed from competing in China's data center computing/compute market, and our effective foreclosure from the China market helped our competitors build larger developer and customer ecosystems to challenge us worldwide.

Unless we are able to return with a product that meets the approval of both the USG and the Chinese government, our lost opportunity and the benefit to our competitors will have a material and adverse impact on our business, operating results, and financial condition.

In April 2025, the USG informed us that a license is required for export to China (including Hong Kong and Macau) and D:5 countries, or to companies headquartered or with an ultimate parent therein, of our H20 integrated circuits and any other circuits achieving the H20's memory bandwidth, interconnect bandwidth, or combination thereof. As a result of these requirements, we incurred a $4.5 billion charge in the first quarter of fiscal year 2026 associated with H20 for excess inventory and purchase obligations.

insights.summary: NVIDIA delivered exceptional Q2 FY2026 results with $46.7B revenue (+56% YoY, +6% QoQ) and $26.4B net income (+59% YoY), driven by surging demand for Blackwell AI and data center accelerated computing platforms. Strong gross margins of 72.4% and operating cash flow of $42.8B demonstrate robust profitability and cash generation, though management faces regulatory headwinds around export controls and supply chain complexity. The company maintains pricing power with large cloud service providers representing ~50% of data center revenue, but faces customer concentration risk with top two direct customers representing 39% of Q2 revenue.
keyQuotes: Revenue was $46.7 billion, up 56% from a year ago and up 6% sequentially. Data Center revenue was $41.1 billion, up 56% from a year ago and up 5% sequentially. The strong year-on-year and sequential growth was driven by demand for our accelerated computing platform used for large language models, recommendation engines, and generative and agentic AI applications.

We continue to ramp our Blackwell architecture, which grew 17% sequentially, including our newest architecture, Blackwell Ultra. We recognized Blackwell revenue across all customer categories, led by large cloud service providers, which represented approximately 50% of Data Center revenue.

Networking revenue was $7.3 billion, up 98% from a year ago and up 46% sequentially, driven by the growth of NVLink compute fabric for GB200 and GB300 systems, the ramp of XDR InfiniBand products, and adoption of Ethernet for AI solutions at cloud service providers and consumer internet companies.

The company faces material headwinds from regulatory restrictions on its China business and uncertainty around forthcoming replacement export rules, which management warns could foreclose its ability to compete in China's data center market. insights.summary: NVIDIA delivered exceptional Q3 FY2024 results with revenue of $18.12 billion (up 206% YoY, 34% QoQ) and net income of $9.24 billion (51% net margin), driven by explosive demand for Data Center AI accelerators particularly H100 Hopper GPUs. The company maintains strong pricing power and a dominant market position in AI infrastructure, though faces near-term headwinds from U.S. export controls to China expected to reduce revenue by 20-25% of Data Center sales in Q4. Management projects continued strong demand visibility through FY2025 with significant supply chain expansion underway.
keyQuotes: Demand for our data center systems and products has surged over the last three quarters and our demand visibility extends into next year.

Data Center revenue was up 279% from a year ago and up 41% sequentially. Strong sales of the NVIDIA HGX platform were driven by global demand for the training and inferencing of large language models, recommendation engines, and generative AI applications.

Our sales to China and other affected destinations, derived from products that are now subject to licensing requirements, have consistently contributed approximately 20-25% of Data Center revenue over the past few quarters. We expect that our sales to these destinations will decline significantly in the fourth quarter of fiscal year 2024, though we believe the decline will be more than offset by strong growth in other regions.

insights.summary: NVIDIA delivered exceptional Q2 FY2024 results with revenue of $13.5B (+101% YoY) and net income of $6.2B (+843% YoY), driven by explosive data center demand for AI/large language models. Gross margins expanded dramatically to 70.1% from 43.5% YoY, reflecting favorable product mix and reduced inventory provisions. Strong forward demand visibility and expanded supplier commitments indicate management confidence, though supply chain complexity and geopolitical export restrictions present execution risks.
keyQuotes: Demand for our data center systems and products has surged over the last two quarters and our demand visibility extends into next year.

Data Center revenue was up 171% from a year ago and up 141% sequentially, led by CSPs and large consumer internet companies. Strong demand for the NVIDIA HGX platform based on our Hopper and Ampere GPU architectures was primarily driven by the development of large language models and generative AI.

In order to meet this demand, we have increased our purchase obligations with existing suppliers, added new suppliers and entered into prepaid supply and capacity agreements. These increased purchase volumes and number of suppliers may create more supply chain complexity and execution risk.
